chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Muhammad ibn 'Arfah, who said: I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying:
When a man leaves enjoining good and restraining from evil, let him be prepared.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (Imam al-Rida, peace be upon him)
key_terms.فَلْیَأْذَنْ: Let him be prepared / Let him know

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of neglecting enjoining good and forbidding evil in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) warns that neglecting the fundamental duty of 'Amr bil-Ma'roof and 'Nahy 'anil Munkar invites divine punishment, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence as a communal obligation (Fard al-Kifaya). This narration from *Thawab al-Amal* underscores that moral stagnation is not merely a personal failing but a breach of covenant with Allah, necessitating spiritual vigilance to maintain the community's ethical integrity.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ridha narrates that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) said, “When my community stops enjoining good and restraining from evil, it should be prepared to wage war against Allah, hallowed be His name.”
